reading.body:
CyrusOne Somerset (NYM1) publishes 23 MW of IT capacity across 185,000 square feet, making it 20.7 percent of New Jersey's disclosed data center power and second in the state by published capacity.

Only five of 48 mapped data centers in New Jersey publish power figures, and those five total 111.3 MW. Somerset's 23 MW is therefore a large share of what is publicly known, but the state's actual inventory is undercounted because most facilities do not disclose power. At 40 kW per rack the site would hold roughly 575 racks, while at 80 kW per rack it would hold roughly 290, so its usefulness for dense AI training depends on rack configuration that is not published.

For AI scaling, 23 MW is modest compared with hyperscale clusters, but the campus sits near the New York metro market and the northern New Jersey grid, which may make it relevant for distributed inference or smaller training jobs. The data does not include tenant mix, actual power consumption, certifications, or announced expansions, so it cannot show whether this facility currently serves AI workloads or will grow to do so.
